# KeyCream

> KeyCream is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app written in Swift that plays mechanical keyboard sounds for every keystroke. It ships seven sound packs recorded from real switches and reads Mechvibes-format packs.

Download KeyCream-x.y.z.zip from https://github.com/halitsever/keycream/releases/latest, move it to Applications and allow it under Privacy & Security > Input Monitoring. It needs macOS 14 or later and runs on Apple Silicon and Intel Macs.

## Docs

- [Installation](https://projects.halit.org/keycream/guide/installation): download, first launch, Input Monitoring permission and updates
- [Using KeyCream](https://projects.halit.org/keycream/guide/usage): the menu, the settings window, languages and lowering the volume during calls
- [Sound packs](https://projects.halit.org/keycream/guide/sound-packs): the bundled packs, their sources and how to add a Mechvibes pack
- [Privacy](https://projects.halit.org/keycream/guide/privacy): what the app reads and stores, and what goes online
- [Troubleshooting](https://projects.halit.org/keycream/guide/troubleshooting): fixes for common problems
- [Building from source](https://projects.halit.org/keycream/guide/building): build script options, releases and the website
- [KeyCream vs Klack vs Mechvibes](https://projects.halit.org/keycream/guide/keycream-vs-klack-vs-mechvibes): price, sound packs, platforms and where each app is stronger, checked 18 November 2026
